cf.title: GIN pageinspect support for entry tree and non-leaf posting tree

input.subject: GIN pageinspect support for entry tree and posting tree

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated, the cost stays inside pageinspect, and the page-level shape answers the concern recorded in P1. Two fixable level 2 points remain, standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2, both about output columns that pageinspect 1.14 would fix as a user-facing contract. A committer would likely want them settled before commit, but neither requires a different proposal.

brief.title: pageinspect functions for GIN entry tree and posting tree internal pages
brief.problem: pageinspect can decode only GIN posting tree leaf pages, through gin_leafpage_items. Users who study GIN storage or fix corrupted GIN indexes cannot see entry tree pages or posting tree internal pages. The author cites education and corruption repair as uses.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds two functions in a new pageinspect 1.14 extension version. gin_entrypage_items decodes entry tree leaf and internal pages, including keys of multi-column indexes, and gin_datapage_items decodes posting tree internal pages. It follows the one-function-per-page-type style of the hash and BRIN functions and rejects metapages, fast list pages and data pages with an error.
user_visible_surface: New function gin_entrypage_items(page bytea, reloid oid) returns setof record with columns itemoffset, downlink, tids, keys.
New function gin_datapage_items(page bytea) returns setof record with columns itemoffset, downlink, item_tid.
pageinspect extension version moves from 1.13 to 1.14.
New error messages when either function gets a metapage, fast list page, data page or non-GIN index.
author_claims: The functions help with education and with corruption repair on GIN indexes.
Separate functions per page type match the existing hash and BRIN pageinspect design.
The patch handles NULL keys after a fix found in review, with tests added.
Output differs between 32-bit and 64-bit builds because GIN aligns the posting list offset on the platform, so an alternative expected file covers 32-bit.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Borodin, Peter Eisentraut, Chao Li, Japin Li and Roman Khapov reviewed it, and the entry reached Ready for Committer, then went back for a missing TupleDescFinalize() call after commit c456e391138. Japin Li posted a rebased v20260901 with that fix, and no committer has replied yet.
unclear: On entry tree leaf pages the downlink column shows raw encoded offset and count values, and the docs do not explain how to read them.
The docs do not describe the output columns or how the keys column formats types and NULL keys.
The proposal does not say what users should use for fast list pages, which both functions reject.
The posting tree internal page test depends on the 8 KiB block size, and the thread accepts this without a fix.
No reviewer or committer reports testing the functions on corrupted pages.

prior_attempts.title: Pageinspect - add functions on GIN and GiST indexes from gevel
prior_attempts.who_objected: Alexander Korotkov, Tomas Vondra, Ashutosh Sharma, Peter Eisentraut
prior_attempts.quote: The proposed patch uses a very different approach, reading the whole index, not individual pages. Why should it be part of pageinspect?
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers said the functions read the whole index, while pageinspect inspects single pages, so the code belongs in a new extension or should be rewritten as page-level functions. Peter Eisentraut also found that the patch no longer compiled and that the stats functions returned one formatted text value where they should return a row with columns. The author planned a new contrib module but posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after three weeks of waiting on the author.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 moved gevel's whole-index functions into pageinspect. This proposal decodes one raw page per call through get_raw_page, which is the page-level shape the P1 reviewers asked for.

prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane listed open issues before the patch could be committed: no documentation update, no simple way to ask for all remaining pages (a count one too large raises an error), and a regression test that depends on tuple layout. objections.title: Output columns encode on-disk details that later fixes cannot change
objections.failure_scenario: A user reads downlink (2147483696,3) on an entry leaf page as a block number and goes looking for block 2147483696. A script that compares output across machines gets a different value on 32-bit builds. Once pageinspect 1.14 ships, changing these columns needs another extension version and an upgrade script.
objections.argument: Message #1 says the leaf downlink has a different meaning from the internal one but is shown the same way, and message #10 confirms it varies by platform. The column named downlink is a tid in gin_entrypage_items but an integer in gin_datapage_items. gin_entrypage_items takes reloid oid, while gist_page_items takes regclass. The doc hunk shows examples only and gives no column definitions.
objections.author_must_show: Can leaf tuples report a decoded posting list offset and item count, or a posting tree root block, instead of the raw tid, and why does downlink differ in type between the two functions?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms the leaf downlink is a raw encoded value shown as a tid, and message #10 confirms it varies by platform. The doc hunk defines no columns, and no reviewer raised the column shape, so the thread does not answer this.

objections.title: keys column format and NULL categories are not defined
objections.failure_scenario: A user repairing a corrupted index sees y=NULL and cannot tell a NULL array element from a NULL array or an empty array, which GIN stores as different key categories. Tools that parse keys from gist_page_items cannot reuse that code, because the format differs.
objections.argument: GIN stores separate null categories, and message #35 shows only the planned output y=NULL. The material does not say whether the keys column keeps the categories apart. gist_page_items prints keys in the index value description style, and this proposal adds a new attname=value text form without saying why.
objections.author_must_show: How does the keys column show each GIN null category and multi-column keys, and why not use the key format gist_page_items already prints?

critic.reasoning: GIN stores three null categories, and the thread and doc hunk show only y=NULL without saying whether the keys column tells them apart. The gist_page_items format comparison is weak support, because pageinspect output formats already differ by access method.

refuted.title: Leaf entry page downlink column exposes raw encoded values
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA repairing a corrupted GIN index runs gin_entrypage_items on an entry tree leaf page and sees downlink (2147483696,3). They read it as a block number and offset, which is wrong. Once 1.14 ships, fixing the column means another extension version and a changed output shape.
refuted.argument: Message #1 states that the leaf-page downlink means something different, encoding a flag, a posting offset and an item count, and that the patch does not handle it differently. The value also differs between 32-bit and 64-bit builds (messages #9 and #10). The documentation hunk shows only an internal-page example, and no reviewer in the thread raised the column shape. The pageinspect output columns become a user-facing contract, and corruption repair is one of the stated uses, so this column should be readable before it is fixed in 1.14.
refuted.author_must_show: Could leaf pages report the posting offset, item count and posting-tree flag as separate named columns, with downlink left NULL, before the 1.14 output shape is fixed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers the same raw leaf downlink and also the type difference between the two functions.

touch_points.reason: pageinspect moves from 1.13 to 1.14 with two new SQL functions, and patch 0003 moves the IS_INDEX macro to pageinspect.h.

touch_points.reason: The functions decode raw pages and run type output functions on keys; the thread does not show whether the 1.13--1.14 script revokes execute from PUBLIC.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The output columns become a contract, and the tests need a 32-bit expected file and assume the 8 KiB block size.

questions: Can gin_entrypage_items report the posting list offset, item count and posting tree root block for leaf tuples as decoded values instead of a raw tid such as (2147483696,3)?
Why is the downlink column a tid in gin_entrypage_items and an integer in gin_datapage_items?
How does the keys column show each GIN null category (null key, empty item, null item), and can a user tell them apart?
Will the documentation define each output column, including what tids and downlink mean on leaf pages versus internal pages?
Has anyone run both functions on deliberately corrupted pages, given that corruption repair is a stated use?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the GIN page layout and pageinspect conventions would have to own it. Peter Eisentraut is credited as co-author in the commit message, but the brief says no committer has replied to the latest version.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the output columns of two functions in pageinspect 1.14, for decoding of possibly corrupted pages without crashes, and for tests that depend on platform alignment and block size. Later changes to the columns need a new extension version.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revisions over several months and moved the entry across CommitFests. Japin Li, a reviewer, posted the latest rebase with the TupleDescFinalize() fix.

priority.reason: The patch fills a gap in pageinspect's GIN coverage for people who study or repair GIN indexes, and the cost stays in one contrib module. It reached Ready for Committer after five reviewers and is now waiting for a committer, with two output-shape points still open.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so safety on corrupted pages, the privilege setup in the 1.13--1.14 script and the actual NULL category output could not be checked. Only 3 of 46 messages were visible, so some open points may have been answered in the thread.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Tomas Vondra, Ashutosh Sharma, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the gevel module's functions for GiST, SP-GiST and GIN indexes into pageinspect, with tests and docs. The functions show whole-index statistics, print the tree and its stored objects, and estimate GIN value counts and query matches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the functions read the whole index, while pageinspect inspects single pages, so the code belongs in a new extension or should be rewritten as page-level functions. Peter Eisentraut also found that the patch no longer compiled and that the stats functions returned one formatted text value where they should return a row with columns. The author planned a new contrib module but posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after three weeks of waiting on the author.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the GinMaxItemSize calculation so that we fit 3 tuples per page.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the GinMaxItemSize calculation so that we fit 3 tuples per page.
Reverted commit(s): Compress GIN posting lists, for smaller index size.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 36a35c55 changed the divisor from 3 to 6, for no apparent reason.
Reducing GinMaxItemSize like that created a dump/reload hazard: loading a
9.3 database to 9.4 might fail with "index row size XXX exceeds maximum 1352
for index ..." error. Revert the change.

While we're at it, make the calculation slightly more accurate. It used to
divide the available space on page by three, then subtract
sizeof(ItemIdData), and finally round down. That's not totally accurate; the
item pointers for the three items are packed tight right after the page
header, but there is alignment padding after the item pointers. Change the
calculation to reflect that, like BTMaxItemSize does. I tested this with
different block sizes on systems with 4- and 8-byte alignment, and the value
after the final MAXALIGN_DOWN was the same with both methods on all
configurations. So this does not make any difference currently, but let's be
tidy.

Also add a comment explaining what the macro does.

This fixes bug #12292 reported by Robert Thaler. Backpatch to 9.4, where the
bug was introduced.

precedents_retrieved.title: use AV work items infrastructure for GIN pending list's cleanup
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves GIN pending list cleanup to an autovacuum work item, requested when the list reaches gin_pending_list_limit. Inserts and updates would then no longer pay for the cleanup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Masahiko Sawada pointed out that work items run only after an autovacuum run, so the pending list could grow far past gin_pending_list_limit while the same work item is registered again and again. He suggested a soft limit and a hard limit, removal of duplicate work items, and skipping the item if autovacuum already cleaned the index. The author had no time to finish a revised version, so he marked the entry "Returned with feedback" and planned to resubmit.
matched_queries: GIN fast list pending pages pageinspect
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So if many insertions happen before executing the autovacuum
work item, we will end up greatly exceeding the threshold
(gin_pending_list_limit) and registering the same work item again and
again.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first changed pageinspect's bt_page_stats to return a set of rows covering a range of B-Tree pages, with a pageinspect version bump to 1.11. After review it added a separate function, bt_multi_page_stats, which takes an index, a starting block number and a block count.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane listed open issues before the patch could be committed: no documentation update, no simple way to ask for all remaining pages (a count one too large raises an error), and a regression test that depends on tuple layout. He then showed the test fails on a 32-bit machine. The author did not address this feedback, and Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback after four weeks of inactivity.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fixes a trivial bug in dumped parse/query/plan trees
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the leading space that the node output code writes after the opening parenthesis when it dumps an array field, so "( 1 4)" becomes "(1 4)". The author called the space a bug in the dumped parse, query and plan trees.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson and Tom Lane said the format is intentional and that changing it could break external parsers of the node format. Tom Lane said the space is a skipped minor optimization and that a small saving in isolation does not justify the risk to third-party code. He would accept such breakage only for a large cut in stored parse tree size, about 2X or better.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
While our existing nodeRead code wouldn't have a
problem with removing the extra whitespace, I share your fear that
we could introduce bugs into some third-party code somewhere.

precedents_retrieved.title: GIN fillfactor
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fillfactor storage parameter to GIN indexes so that index build leaves free space on pages, and apply it to the page split ratio in dataPlaceToPageLeaf. The default was debated between 100, which matches the packed 9.4 indexes, and 90.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No benchmark showed that the option improves performance. Heikki Linnakangas tested random updates and found that GIN indexes do not bloat after build, because posting tree pages already keep some free space, so he concluded the option is not useful in practice. Alexander Korotkov showed one case with bloat but agreed it was probably not worth it without real use cases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this, I think we should just drop this patch. It's not useful in
practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add OID descriptions to dumped parse/query/plan trees
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds comments to the text dumps of parse, query and plan trees that name the object behind each OID, such as the index, operator, function or type. It does this by catalog lookups inside the node output code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the lookups would make the dump code need a live, non-aborted transaction and could add catalog accesses that cause problems or deadlocks, so pprint could no longer be called from almost anywhere. He also said the change breaks re-reading of dumped trees, which rules, views and parallel query depend on. The author withdrew the patch after this reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It means that the dump code has to
execute in a live (not-aborted) transaction, which is not a
requirement it had before, and will complicate some debugging
scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: new diagnostic items for the dynamic sql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two PL/pgSQL GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS items that return the text of a dynamic SQL statement that failed to parse and the error position in it. Pavel Stehule suggested the more general names PG_SQL_TEXT and PG_ERROR_LOCATION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled with no further review, and the author's email bounced by August 2022, so nobody was left to carry it. Tom Lane judged the last versions far too invasive for a use case that seemed hypothetical, because a re-RAISE already preserves the query text and position in the client error report. He recommended returning to a definition equal to the PG_DIAG_INTERNAL_QUERY and PG_DIAG_INTERNAL_POSITION fields, returning NULL when they are absent. The entry was returned with feedback in December 2022.

precedents_retrieved.title: brin: avoid errors processing work item following concurrent reindex
precedents_retrieved.summary: When autovacuum processes a BRIN summarize work item for an index that a concurrent REINDEX CONCURRENTLY has dropped, it logs an ERROR. The patch makes brin_summarize_range lock the index OID and use try_relation_open, so it discards the work item silently, or at most reports it at INFO level as vacuum_open_relation does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stalled without agreement on the approach. Alvaro Herrera did not want every work-item handler to silently discard items whose relation is gone. He preferred a transaction-end hook that removes work items for dropped relations, but nobody wrote it and the hook had no clear place to collect the OIDs. In September 2021 he proposed pushing the small fix to all branches, but Justin Pryzby still asked why an INFO message would not do, and the entry was closed with no consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This thread has stalled, and from the discussions there isn't consencus on how to proceed (if at all?), so I'm marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
Reverted commit(s): Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 06f5295 as per issues with this approach, both in
terms of efficiency impact and stability.  First, contrary to the
single-item cache for transaction IDs in transam.c, the cache may finish
by not be hit for a long time, and without an invalidation mechanism to
clear it, it would cause inconsistent results on wraparound for
example.  Second, the use of SubTransGetTopmostTransaction() for the
caching has a limited impact on performance.  SubTransGetParent() could
have more impact, though the benchmarking of the single-item approach
still needs to be proved, particularly under the conditions where SLRU
lookups are stressed in parallel with overflowed snapshots (aka more
than 64 subxids generated, for example).

After discussion with Andres Freund.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent reason still applies. P1 died over whole-index reads, and this proposal is page-level. The P5 concern about 32-bit test layout was handled in messages #10 and #40. P3 has no recorded reason. The thread cites no earlier discussion of GIN entry tree inspection.

No conflict with the SQL standard, pg_dump or GUCs. The proposal adds contrib functions under a normal extension version bump, and the one-function-per-page-type split follows the existing hash and BRIN functions.

The proposal adds two read-only pageinspect functions and an extension version bump. It changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or core ABI, so it needs nothing from pg_upgrade or replication. The 32-bit and 64-bit output difference comes from the existing GIN page layout, which the patch only reads. Whether decoding corrupted pages is safe depends on the code and was not checked.

The proposal adds no new privilege path that I can find. pageinspect is superuser-only by convention, and both functions take raw pages from get_raw_page, which already checks privileges and blocks other sessions' temp tables (message #4). The thread does not show whether the 1.13--1.14 script revokes execute from PUBLIC. gin_entrypage_items also runs type output functions on keys read from a page that may be corrupted, which gist_page_items already does. A committer would likely check both points in the code, which I cannot see.

From the maintenance and fit angle the proposal is sound. It is page-level, unlike [P1], it costs nothing for users who do not install it, and it follows the existing hash and BRIN style. Peter Eisentraut contributed code, but no committer has taken ownership.

No existing Postgres feature decodes GIN entry tree pages or posting tree internal pages. pageinspect's gin_metapage_info, gin_page_opaque_info and gin_leafpage_items cover other page types, and amcheck's GIN check validates pages without showing their contents. The gevel extension in [P1] works on whole indexes, not single pages, so it does not do this job, and the patch extends pageinspect's existing per-page-type mechanism without adding a second one.

No demand objection. pageinspect already decodes every page type for btree, hash, BRIN and GiST, so filling the GIN gap matches existing coverage, and Andrey Borodin called it useful in message #3. The cost stays inside one contrib module and reaches only people who install it; the corruption-repair use is asserted, not shown.
